tests.name: Wall squat mobility
tests.thresholds: inches from wall, lower is better: L1<=12, L2<=6, L3<=2
howToTest: Stand facing a wall, feet shoulder-width, arms straight overhead.
Start with toes 12 inches from the wall. Squat until thighs are below knee height, then stand up.
It doesn’t count if your hands, face or knees touch the wall, your heels lift, or you tip backward.
Passed? Move 2 inches closer and try again. Log the closest distance you passed.

Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Broad jump
tests.thresholds: inches, higher is better: L1>=height, L2>=height+12, L3>=height+24
howToTest: Stand with toes behind a line, feet together.
Swing your arms and jump forward as far as you can. Land on both feet.
Measure from the line to the back of your closest heel.
Take 3 tries. Log your best one.

Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Trap bar deadlift
tests.thresholds: lb for 5 reps, higher is better: L1>=1.5*bodyweight, L2>=2*bodyweight, L3>=2.5*bodyweight
howToTest: Stand inside the trap bar, grab the handles, chest up, back flat.
Stand up tall, then lower with control. That’s 1 rep.
Warm up with lighter sets, adding weight until 5 reps is hard but your form stays good.
Log the heaviest weight you lifted 5 times in a row.

Foundation -> Level 1: Trap bar deadlift 5×5, add 5–10 lb each week
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Wall sit
tests.thresholds: seconds: L1 = both-leg hold>=60; L2 = single-leg hold>=30; L3 = single-leg hold>=60 (single-leg uses weaker leg)
howToTest: Logged as two parts: both legs, then one leg.
See the ⓘ on each part for how it’s done.

Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Wall sit, both legs
howToTest: Back flat on a wall, slide down until thighs are level with the floor and knees are over ankles.
Hands off your legs.
Time stops when you stand up or slide down.

tests.name: Wall sit, one leg
howToTest: Same wall sit position, then lift one foot off the floor.
Time it on each leg, resting in between.
Log the shorter of the two times.

tests.name: Bench press
tests.note: Reps with bar at your bodyweight
howToTest: Load the bar to your bodyweight (round down to the nearest 5 lb).
Lower to your chest, press to straight arms. No bouncing.
A spotter must stand behind you every set.
Log how many clean reps you did without racking the bar.

Level 2 -> Level 3: Add 5 total reps at bodyweight each week
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Pull-ups
howToTest: Hang with straight arms, palms facing away.
Pull until your chin is over the bar, then lower all the way down.
No swinging or kicking.
Log how many full reps you did.

Level 1 -> Level 2: Half your max, 5 times a day
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Hand-release push-ups
howToTest: Lie flat on your chest, hands next to your shoulders.
Lift your hands off the floor for a moment, put them back down.
Push up to straight arms, body in a straight line. That’s 1 rep.
Go without stopping. Log your total.

Level 2 -> Level 3: 100 reps for time, once a week
2 max sets at the end of training
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Farmer's carry
tests.note: Dumbbells adding up to your bodyweight
howToTest: Pick two dumbbells that add up to your bodyweight. A 220 lb man uses 110 lb in each hand.
Stand tall and walk at a steady pace.
Stop when you put them down.
Log the distance in feet. The lane is marked every 50 ft.

Level 1 -> Level 2: Farmer’s carry at 80% of bodyweight 4×100 ft
Level 2 -> Level 3: Farmer’s carry at 110% of bodyweight 5×50 ft
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Dead hang
howToTest: Grab the pull-up bar, palms facing away.
Hang with straight arms, feet off the floor.
Time stops when you let go.

Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Plank
howToTest: Forearms and toes on the floor, elbows under shoulders.
Body straight from head to heels. Squeeze your glutes and stomach.
Time stops when your hips sag or knees touch.

Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: 800m run
howToTest: 800 metres is 2 laps of a running track, or 0.8 km on the treadmill.
On a treadmill, set the incline to 1%.
Run it as fast as you can. Log your time.

Foundation -> Level 1: Zone 2 walk or ruck 30 min, twice a week
Level 1 -> Level 2: Run 200 m at goal pace 6 times, 90 sec rest
Run 400 m 4 times, just faster than goal pace
Level 2 -> Level 3: Run 600 m at goal pace 3 times, 3 min rest
Run 200 m faster than goal pace 8 times
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Assault bike, 25 cal
howToTest: Set the bike screen to count calories.
On “go”, push and pull as hard as you can.
Stop the clock when the screen reads 25 calories. Log your time.

Level 1 -> Level 2: Bike 10 cal 5 times, 1 min rest between
Bike 15 cal 3 times at goal pace, 2 min rest
Level 2 -> Level 3: Bike 25 cal 4 times, 3 min rest between
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Sled push
howToTest: Load the sled so plates plus sled weigh about your bodyweight. A 200 lb man uses about 200 lb total.
Hands on the tall handles, arms straight, body leaning forward.
On “go”, drive the sled 50 ft with short, fast steps.
Log your time. Same sled and same floor every test day, so times are fair.

Level 1 -> Level 2: Sled push at 75% of bodyweight 6×50 ft
Level 2 -> Level 3: Sled push at bodyweight 5×50 ft, 90 sec rest
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

tests.name: Sled pull
tests.note: Half bodyweight on the sled, 50 ft
howToTest: Load the sled to about half your bodyweight. A 200 lb man uses about 100 lb total.
Hold the straps or rope handles in front of you, arms straight. Sit back into a half squat.
On “go”, walk backward and drag the sled 50 ft. Keep your arms straight and chest up.
Log your time.

Level 1 -> Level 2: Backward sled drag at 40% of bodyweight 6×50 ft
Level 2 -> Level 3: Backward sled drag at half bodyweight 5×50 ft, 90 sec rest
Hold Level 3: One hard attempt at the test every 2 weeks
Keep its main exercise in your week, with fewer sets
Spend the extra time on your weakest test

drills: Calf stretch off a step 2×45 sec

hip.buttonLabel: Feet turned out or knees caved in
hip.explanation: Feet turning out or knees caving in means tight hips.

upper.buttonLabel: Arms dropped or chest fell forward
upper.explanation: Arms dropping or chest falling forward means a stiff upper back or shoulders.

glossary.explanation: Easy, steady cardio where you can still talk in full sentences. A brisk walk, a ruck or an easy bike. It builds your engine without wearing you out.
A walk carrying a backpack with weight in it. Start with 20–30 lb.
The speed you need to hit your next level’s time. For the 800m Level 1 (3:15), that’s 200 m in about 49 sec.
85% of the heaviest weight you can lift 5 times. If your best is 300 lb, use about 255 lb.
A little under your bodyweight. A 200 lb man would use 170–180 lb on the bar.
The total weight compared to what you weigh. For a 200 lb man, 80% is 160 lb. On a carry, split it between both hands (80 lb each). On a sled, count the sled plus plates.
Hold one dumbbell or kettlebell against your chest. Sit down between your knees, chest up, then stand.
Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Push through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from knees to shoulders. Lower slowly.
Jump onto a sturdy box (12–20 in high), land softly. Step down, don’t jump down.
Land and hold completely still for 2 seconds before moving.
Hold a light trap bar (about a quarter of your deadlift weight). Jump straight up, land softly, reset.
One foot forward, one foot back. Lower your back knee toward the floor, then stand. A “hold” means you pause at the bottom for the time given.
Upper back on a bench, barbell across your hips (use a pad). Push your hips up until your body is flat, squeeze, lower.
The same lift as the test. “Heavy” means a weight you can lift about 3 times.
Lie on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Press up to straight arms, lower to chest level.
Hold a light resistance band at shoulder height, arms straight. Pull it apart until it touches your chest. Keeps shoulders healthy.
A bench press where you hold the bar still on your chest for 2 seconds before pressing up.
On parallel bars, lower until your shoulders are a little below your elbows, then press up. Loop a band under your knees if you need help.
Do as many reps as you can. Rack, rest 15 sec, do more. Rest 15 sec, do more. Those three pieces are one set.
Bench press with hands shoulder-width apart. Works the back of the arms harder.
Jump or step up so your chin is over the bar. Lower yourself as slowly as you can, about 5 seconds. Each lowering is 1 rep.
Loop a resistance band over the bar and put a knee or foot in it. The band takes some of your weight.
Set a bar at waist height. Lie under it, grab it, body straight, heels on the floor. Pull your chest to the bar.

glossary.term: Half your max, 5 times a day
matches: Half your max, 5 times a day
glossary.explanation: If your best is 8 pull-ups, do sets of 4. Do a set 5 times through the day, hours apart. Never to failure. It trains the movement like a skill.
Add load: a dip belt with a plate, a dumbbell between your feet, or a backpack. Start with 10 lb.
Hang with straight arms. Without bending your elbows, pull your shoulder blades down to lift yourself an inch. Lower and repeat.
Do 1 rep, rest briefly, then 2, then 3, up to 5. That’s one round. Start again at 1.
Set a 10-min timer. Do as many pull-ups as you can in small sets with short rests. Write down the total and beat it next time.
Push-ups with your hands on a bench or box. Easier than the floor. Lower the height as you get stronger.
Take 4 seconds to lower to the floor, then push up normally.
At a cable machine, keep elbows at your sides and push the bar or rope down until your arms are straight.
Start a 10-min timer. At the start of each minute, do the reps, then rest until the next minute starts.
Push-ups with hands closer than shoulder-width. Works the back of the arms.
Do 2 reps, rest briefly, then 4, 6, 8, 10, then back down: 8, 6, 4, 2.
Do it as fast as you can. Write down how long it took and beat it next time.
Carry one heavy dumbbell in one hand like a suitcase. Stand tall, don’t lean. Switch hands each set.
One hand and knee on a bench. Pull a dumbbell up to your hip with the other hand, lower slowly.
Hold heavy dumbbells at your sides. Lift your shoulders toward your ears, hold 1 second, lower.
Drape a towel over the pull-up bar and hang holding both ends. Much harder on your grip.
Pinch two weight plates together, smooth sides out, and hold them at your side.
Pick up heavy dumbbells and just hold them, standing still.
Hang from the pull-up bar with straight arms as long as the time given.
Hang with one hand. Keep the other lightly on a towel or band for help.
Kettlebell between your feet. Push your hips back, grab it with a flat back, stand tall. Teaches the hinge.
Hold the bar at your hips, knees soft. Push your hips back and slide the bar down your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch, then stand.
On the back extension bench, lower your upper body, then lift until your body is straight.
Sets of 2 reps with a weight close to your max. Do 3–5 sets.
Trap bar deadlift while standing on a 1–2 inch plate, so you lift from lower down.
Deadlift with the plates raised on blocks, so the lift is shorter and you can handle more weight.
Lie on your back, arms up, knees bent over your hips. Slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg. Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
On hands and knees, stretch out one arm and the opposite leg. Hold 2 seconds, switch.
On one forearm, feet stacked, body straight sideways. Don’t let your hips drop.
Kneel holding the wheel. Roll forward as far as you can control, then roll back.
A plank with your elbows further out in front of your shoulders. Much harder.
Lie on your back, arms overhead. Lift your shoulders and legs a few inches, lower back pressed down. Hold.
Forearms and toes, body straight from head to heels. Squeeze your glutes and stomach.
Squat down as low as you comfortably can with no weight, then stand.
A wall sit with one foot lifted off the floor.
Back flat against a wall, thighs level with the floor, knees over ankles. Hold.
Loop a heavy band around something solid and behind your knees. Lean back into the band and sit into a squat. Easy on the knees.
Stand on one leg in front of a box. Sit back until you touch the box, stand up on the same leg.
Same as single-leg box squat, using a lower box.
Step onto a knee-height box holding dumbbells. Drive through the top foot to stand up.
Run 20 seconds, building to fast but relaxed. Walk back. Do these after an easy session.
Hold the sled straps with straight arms, sit back into a half squat, and walk backward with small steps. Easy on the knees.
Stand facing the sled, holding the straps. Row your hands to your ribs to pull the sled toward you, then walk back and repeat.
Tie a rope to the sled and walk it out. Stand still and pull it in toward you, one hand over the other.
Push a light sled as fast as you can. Fast feet, low body.
Lean into the sled handles with straight arms and drive it forward with short, powerful steps. Use the weight written.
Lean into the sled handles with straight arms and drive it forward with short, powerful steps.
As hard as you possibly can.
Go hard for 20 sec, then pedal easily for 40 sec. That’s one round.
Half-kneel facing a wall, front toes about 4 in away. Push the front knee forward to touch the wall without lifting your heel.
Stand on a step on the balls of your feet. Let your heels drop below the step and hold.
A goblet squat with your heels on a small plate. Lets you sit deeper while your ankles loosen up.
Sit with both knees bent at right angles, one leg in front, one to the side. Rotate your knees to switch sides.
On hands and knees, slide your knees wide apart. Rock your hips back gently and hold.
A small loop band just above your knees. Push your knees out against it as you squat.
Back and arms against a wall, arms in a “goal post”. Slide your arms up keeping them touching the wall, then back down.
Lie on your side, knees bent, arms out in front. Open your top arm across to the other side and follow it with your eyes.
Foam roller across your upper back, hands behind your head. Lean back over the roller, then sit up. Move it up an inch and repeat.
Hold a broomstick overhead with a wide grip, arms straight. Squat as deep as you can, keeping the stick over your head.
The test itself, practised. Stand facing a wall a few inches away, arms overhead, and squat slowly without touching it.
Wide stance. Shift your weight to one side and bend that knee, keeping the other leg straight with toes up.
Hands under shoulders, body straight. Lower your chest to the floor and push back up.
The test itself. Jump forward from both feet, land on both.
Pedal until the screen shows that many calories, as a hard effort. Then rest as written.
A track lap is 400 m. On a treadmill, watch the distance. Run the set distance, then rest as written.
Walk holding a heavy dumbbell in each hand, standing tall.

howlog.title: Logging on test day
howlog.text: Enter today’s date and your bodyweight. Weigh in at the gym. Do the tests in any order. After each one, tap its box and scroll to your result. Skipped a test? Leave it. Entered one by mistake? Tap it and choose Clear. Tap Save results at the bottom when you’re done. You can save more than once on the same day and it updates that day’s results. Not sure how a test works? Tap the i next to it.

bw.title: Why bodyweight?
bw.text: Three tests are set by what you weigh: bench press, deadlift and farmer’s carry. Weigh in on test day so your targets are accurate.

height.title: Why height?
height.text: The broad jump target is based on your height. Level 1 is jumping your own height. You only enter it once.

levels.title: How levels work
levels.text: Every test has three levels. Each level is harder than the one before. Foundation: not at Level 1 yet. Everyone starts somewhere. Level 1, 2, 3: you passed that standard. The bars next to each test show your level: means Level 2. Gold bars mean Level 3.

overall.title: Your overall level
overall.text: Your overall level is your lowest test. Example: Level 2 on everything except pull-ups at Level 1 means you’re Level 1 overall. This keeps you balanced. Fix your weakest test and your overall level goes up. It shows “In progress” until you’ve done all 14 tests.

score.title: Your score
score.text: Each test gives you points: Foundation = 0, Level 1 = 1, Level 2 = 2, Level 3 = 3. 14 tests × 3 points = 42 points maximum. Watch this number go up each test day.

plans.title: Picking a plan
plans.text: Each test has a plan for every step: Reach L1: for Foundation. Gets you to Level 1. Reach L2: you’re at Level 1, working to Level 2. Reach L3: you’re at Level 2, working to Level 3. Keep L3: you’ve made it. Hold it. The app picks your plan from your latest test. Tap another to look ahead. Tap any underlined word to see how the exercise is done.

week.title: Your 3 workouts
week.text: You train 3 times a week . Each workout is already built for you from your test results. Leg Day : legs, jumping and mobility Upper Body Day : pushing and pulling Grip & Cardio Day : grip, core and fitness Leave a rest day between them. Monday, Wednesday, Friday works well, but any 3 days with a day off in between is fine. Open the workout, warm up, then do the exercises top to bottom. Your weakest test comes first, while you’re fresh. About 50–60 minutes. When you log a new test, the workouts update by themselves.

warmup.title: Warm-up
warmup.text: 10 minutes before every session: 5 min easy on the bike or treadmill, then 5 min of the mobility drills from your wall squat plan. After 40, joints and tendons need this. Don’t skip it.

deload.title: Every 4th week, go lighter
deload.text: Weeks 1, 2 and 3: train as planned. Week 4: do the same exercises with half the sets and lighter weights. Then start again. Your body gets stronger while it recovers. This is how you keep progressing without getting hurt.

cardio.title: Extra cardio
cardio.text: On 1 or 2 rest days, do 30–45 minutes of Zone 2: easy, steady cardio where you can still talk. A brisk walk, a ruck (walking with a weighted backpack) or an easy bike ride. It improves your 800m and bike times and helps you recover.

between.title: Between test days
between.text: Don’t test your maxes in training. Train hard but leave 1–2 reps in the tank. Save your all-out effort for test day.

coachinfo.title: Extra work from Zaki
coachinfo.text: Zaki added these exercises just for you, on top of your normal plan. Do them as written. Tap any underlined word to see how it’s done. If something doesn’t feel right, tell Zaki.

coachhow.title: Assigning exercises
coachhow.text: Pick a brother from the list. Type an exercise. Start typing to pick from the app’s exercise list, or write your own. Add a note if it helps, like “every morning” or “before Day A”. Tap Add . It shows up at the top of his Train screen right away. Only you can see this screen. Each brother only sees his own exercises.

coachgrid.title: Reading the group table
coachgrid.text: One row per brother, showing his latest test. F = Foundation (not at Level 1 yet) L1, L2, L3 = level reached — = skipped that test Swipe sideways to see every test. Tap a name to see his progress and assign him exercises. Copy all copies every test from every brother, one row per test day, ready to paste into Excel or Google Sheets.
